name: orb_wide_range_fade_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is wider than 2x the 20-day average ORB range, the initial move has over-extended — the opening auction was dominated by emotional retail order flow, and institutional mean-reversion will pull price back toward the ORB midpoint. Wide opening ranges are the OPPOSITE of compression — they represent exhaustion at the extremes. Instead of buying the breakout, fade the wide range by selling near ORB_high and buying near ORB_low. This is contrarian to standard ORB strategies and profits from the ~60% of wide-range days where price mean-reverts to the range midpoint. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB logic always buys breakouts, even when the opening range itself is a breakout (from overnight levels).
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; today's 15-min ORB range > 2x avg_ORB_range_20d
indicators: price_position = (close - ORB_low_15) / ORB_range_15  # 0 at low, 1 at high

conditions: RSI_14 < 25 (oversold at bottom of wide range)
long.confirmation: price bounces from ORB_low area (close > open on entry bar, price_position rising for 2 bars)

conditions: RSI_14 > 75 (overbought at top of wide range)
short.confirmation: price rejects from ORB_high area (close < open on entry bar, price_position falling for 2 bars)

entry.entry_price: limit order at price_position 0.10 (long) or 0.90 (short) within ORB range

exit.target: ORB_mid (midpoint of wide range — mean reversion target)
exit.stop_loss: close beyond ORB extreme by 0.2 * ORB_range_15 (range extension) OR 0.4% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 30% of target reached, trail at 15% progress level
exit.signal_exit: if ORB_high/low is broken by > 0.3 * ORB_range (range extension, not fading), exit immediately

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX wide ranges may continue expanding
filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-11:00 IST; wide range fading works best when institutions arrive post-open
filters.volume_filter: opening 15-min volume > 1.5x average (confirming wide range was driven by real flow)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (>2%); on strong trend days, wide ranges continue
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip if wide range driven by stock-specific news (earnings surprise, analyst action) — news-driven wide ranges don't fade
other_filters: wide_range threshold 2.0x must be robust; consider 1.8x for more signals at cost of lower win rate

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — wide range fading is contrarian and goes against standard ORB doctrine, so it's less crowded

weaknesses: Fading wide ranges is contrarian; when the wide range IS the breakout (news-driven, institutional-driven), the fade loses big as price extends the range
Wide range days are infrequent (~10-15% of sessions), making this a low-frequency supplement strategy
The ORB midpoint target may not be reached on days where price consolidates near the extreme instead of reverting, resulting in time-stop exits with small losses
prior_art: Crabel (1990) wide range days (WR4/WR7); Connors (1999) on fading extended ranges. Adapted from daily chart concept to 15-min intraday opening range.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 40bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 24.8 - 13.3 = 11.5bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~2.5bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg, daily ~1.25bps. The 26bps estimate is per wide-range signal day. Strategy needs to be combined with others. The edge is in the mean-reversion nature: wide ranges create natural S/R at extremes.
